what: Prompt R3b (2026-11-16): every change to a NORMAL turn's tool list since fixture v6 (5715254). No tool added, removed or moved; five changed. Undoing the list on v7's tools gives v6's byte for byte (Tests/test_agent_payload_equivalence.py). A draft chat's turn keeps prompts/draft_frozen/tools.json.

changes.why: item 2: the comparison is written by code; it takes a list of two to six ids and a span

description.old: Compare two players under the production model over the latest run's six-gameweek horizon: the horizon sum (the verdict's basis) and the figures for the run's FIRST gameweek (first_gw -- between deadlines that is the gameweek just played, not the next one; note_stale says so). This is the route for comparing two players over the coming weeks ('who's better over the next six weeks'): each side carries the player's FPL status word and chance of playing with the gameweek it is for, so the comparison needs no player card. For 'X or Y this week' prefer compare_predictions, which defaults to the next deadline's gameweek and names the terms behind the gap. Whatever you quote, name its gameweek. available=false means the player cannot play for his club; lead with availability_note.
description.new: Compare two or more players under the production model, written by code: a table with each player's predicted points and fixture gameweek by gameweek, each total, who is ahead and by how much, how the gap moves across the span, the price difference in £m, each player's chance of starting and FPL's flags. Its text is shown to the user as the reply, so write nothing of your own. Pass every player's id in player_ids (two to six, from resolve_player) and, when the user names a number of gameweeks, horizon ('over the next 3 gameweeks' is 3); with no horizon it covers every gameweek the latest update covers from the next deadline's -- the six-gameweek horizon. This is the route for comparing two players over the coming weeks ('who's better over the next six weeks', 'how do X and Y compare'): it carries each player's FPL flag, so the comparison needs no player card. For 'X or Y this week' prefer compare_predictions, which defaults to the next deadline's gameweek and names the terms behind the gap. A result that is an error or carries no code-built text is yours to answer from: whatever you quote, name its gameweek; available=false means the player cannot play for his club; lead with availability_note.

player_ids.description: The players' FPL element ids, two to six, in the order the user named them

horizon.description: Optional: how many gameweeks to compare over, counted from the next deadline's gameweek, 1 to 8 ('the next 3 gameweeks' is 3). Omit for every gameweek the latest update covers

changes.why: item 3: every club, more than five clubs, or the user's own players' clubs -> the code-built table

description.old: which is not the same thing as blank_gameweek; with no team the answer is compact rows (team, gw, opponent, home, attacking, defensive) and the two-numbers rule is stated once at the top. Fixtures beyond
description.new: which is not the same thing as blank_gameweek. For EVERY club (no team), for a list of more than five clubs (teams) or for the clubs of the user's own players (my_players=true -- 'who do my players face') the answer is a table written by code: one row a club, one column a gameweek, each cell the opponent, home or away, and the fixture's two ratings in words, with each club's ratings added up over the span and the next deadline; its text is shown to the user as the reply, so write nothing of your own. Never call this once per club for more than five clubs -- ask for them in ONE call. A list of five clubs or fewer comes back as compact rows (team, gw, opponent, home, attacking, defensive) for you to answer from, the two-numbers rule stated once at the top. Fixtures beyond
